Rayaz (L95)

Scoring-table region: Sarhal.

In one sentence: As the Riverclaw chief chosen by the Naga, organize the scattered lizardfolk tribes, frontier, and waterways before pursuing the prophesied final empire.

Story: medium-high | Mission-tree length: medium-short (16 L95-exclusive missions; the formable is counted separately) | Mission-tree version: current local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: medium-high | Prison difficulty: medium (prophetic legitimacy and prerequisites) | Early pressure: medium-high | Expansion: high, shifting to a larger map after formation

The Chosen of the Naga

Rayaz is a landed Araskayy lizardfolk tribal country in 1444. Its country history gives it Sykar of the Riverclaw family, Naga clerical privilege, rivals on the Taneyas frontier, and historical friendships with Asarta and Arazin. Sykar was already ruler in 1420 and still has a namesake heir in 1444, establishing an independent start rather than a Tag that appears halfway through an Asarta campaign. The Naga regard Sykar as the prophesied forerunner; the final empire remains a contested future.【Local history script】【Local flavour text】

His brother Katyradz starts separately as Asarta. Rayaz’s missions both want the brother to weaken Karassk and fear that a powerful brother may challenge the succession recognized by the Naga. Being chosen is therefore a political burden that must continually be proved. Both countries may later form Khatalashya, but their opening missions and motives remain separate.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

The offline English Wiki has no dedicated Rayaz country-history page. Its Countries during the Greentide list Rayaz among the Riverclaw tribes and Arazin as its vassal; the Anzara Empire page describes later conflict with Rayaz and contains unreconciled end years, 1453 and 1454. This article does not turn either year into an established 1444 fact or replace current formation conditions with a regional Wiki page.【Wiki material】

Foundations from Tribe to Empire

The L95-exclusive tree is short but tightly packed. Sykar must maintain Naga support, integrate neighbouring tribes and vassals, repair frontier routes, and bring river trade and ports into one political network. Frontier smuggling and outside warlords are real pressures in the flavour text, so the missions demand defences, fleets, and local order rather than treating a few conquests as an automatic stable empire.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

Another line is prophetic legitimacy. Naga support provides governing resources while binding Rayaz to religious authority and public expectations. Later missions can reform the government from a tribe into a monarchy and approach the conditions for S81 Khatalashya. The current formation decision is open to multiple eligible predecessors; L95 and L96 remain distinguished by former Tag in some events. The shared imperial continuation must not be counted as Rayaz-exclusive content.【Local script】

The flavour text gives Sykar a concrete dilemma: some profit from addictive Nazni Grass, which he seeks to curb; when facing the Ashhana, he tries to avoid direct slaughter through a gentler response. More radical opposition also appears, so “tries to avoid” is not a completed permanent tolerant institution. Clerical expectations, trade interests, and the safety of conquered peoples collide in the same campaign.【Local flavour text】

Compared with Asarta, Rayaz establishes legitimacy first and turns the tribal coalition into a functioning state. Waterways, clergy, and frontier defence consume early resources. Advice to finish the predecessor tree before forming is useful player experience, not a verified mandatory rule. Players seeking the complete sibling story can treat L95 as a self-contained campaign rather than a tag-change interlude.【Local script】【Community viewpoint】

This also poses a distinctive question for the player: do you want prophecy to give the state an order, or the state to exist only in service of prophecy? Current text includes road-building and curbs on harmful trade, alongside clerical politics and expansionary pressure. The words "chosen one" alone cannot decide how the player balances those demands.【Local flavour text】

Personality and Recommendation

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 86/100 | Authoritarianism 79/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 72/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 60/100) | Pluralism 49/100.

v2.1 values: Neutral (62/100), trajectory mixed. Frontier protection, river trade, and tribal integration provide public benefits; clerical privilege and prophetic competition concentrate power and create risks to local autonomy. Expansion and monarchical reform are not penalized in themselves. The evidence is insufficient to classify this as a country of large-scale institutional harm.

The official Final Empire release announcement discusses Sykar and the sibling split. Two 2026 player discussions cover the fast Khatalashya route and whether to finish L95 missions before changing Tags; the latter remains experience rather than a hard rule. Full sources are on the evidence page.【Official release announcement】【Community viewpoint】

Recommended for players who enjoy lizardfolk prophetic legitimacy, tribal integration, river economies and a quick transition into a formable campaign. Avoid this route if you only want a long predecessor tree or want to escape religious politics. Original research sources and limitations are preserved on the Chinese research evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Racial, government and mission rewards are excluded, and successor sets do not automatically stack with predecessor ideas. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals, not automatically events already completed in 1444. Native English originals are reused rather than back-translating expanded Chinese localisation. Inherited effect-display values and any unresolved unit caveats are retained without changing Chinese source data.

Rayaz (L95) — Rayaz Ideas

Conditional or alternative definitions exist. They are shown separately by applicability; no set is assumed guaranteed or simultaneously stacked.

Traditions: Rayaz Traditions

Effects: Infantry Cost: -10%; Advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Chosen of the Naga

For denouncing the decadent Anzaran emperors in 1400, Zerati nagas were expelled from the country for treason. These refugees dispersed among the local tribes, joining up with their naga structure to plot revenge. Their first step was to look for a candidate capable of enforcing their ambitions. Their search stopped in the house of a Riverclaw chieftain, who brought them in to educate his firstborn. He was just a two year old, sitting and writing today's adventures in his journal. This obviously surprised the nagas, as this was definitely not a normal age to learn how to read and write. But it was a good age to groom their chosen one. The son's name was Sykar. And he was going to be the one to fulfill the naga's ambitions.

Effects: Ruler administrative skill: +1.

Idea 2: Twin Academy

The Twin Academy is a university founded at the entrance of Lasadzanach. There, the minds of the future are educated in two great buildings, connected by a monumental bridge spanning across the Khazynas river. Each side hosts a number of disciplines, the west side teaching the ways of the Sovereign and the east teaching the principles of the Erudite. It’s a place where every layer of lizardfolk society meets, from the poorest to chieftains and emperors - all you have to do is to prove yourself capable enough in the entry exams to become a student of this prestigious establishment.

Effects: Reform progress growth: +10%; Idea cost: -5%.

Idea 3: Making Soldier from a Tribesman

One of the first things that Sykar changed when he became the chieftain was to reform the army from a squabble of tribesmen into an organised force. A proper chain of command, standardised formations, a collective fund to supply the army with bronze weapons. These seemingly common ideas were not familiar to the Rayaz before and these improvements were one of the key reasons why the armies of the Naga coalition were able to hold up against professional, battle-hardened armies of Anzara.

Effects: Discipline: +5%.

Idea 4: Destined Unifiers

Rayaz was the centerpoint of a vulnerable coalition, split between the Riverclaw brothers, who held together their disparate tribal allies through the unifying efforts of the influential Nagas. These tribes with time became impatient and discouraged by the past war against Zerat, which left them on the verge of breaking ties, but one thing stayed their swords. A prophecy of old, depicted three brothers who would lead the lizardfolk into the 333rd empire. The Nagas preached that the Riverclaws were these prophesied leaders and thus the many tribal allies held onto the glorious vision of helping the Unifier in his attempts to form the Final Empire, foretold to be the final one by the Anzalkatsa teachings.

Effects: Diplomatic annexation cost: -15%; Diplomatic vassal acceptance: +10.

Idea 5: People of the River

Here in the jungles of Taneyas, the roads are rare, unmaintained and obsolete, while the rivers are the lifeblood of trade. Confluences are even more important, serving as a natural joining point for traders. On one of these confluences lies the settlement of Razayas, where the most common trade routes between Zerat and Karassk meet. No matter if you're Anzaran or Karassian, Khugran or Asartan or even human, Rayazas merchants can reach you from there and help you reach new markets faster than the sun sets over the treeline.

Effects: Number of merchants: +1.

Idea 6: Expert Trappers

The landscape of the lizardfolk jungles is harsh and unforgiving. You never know what you can step on and your field of view is narrow apart from river crossings. This is a perfect environment for guerilla warfare and it is why the Arraskay tribesmen were able to retain their autonomy from so many empires. A stumble into a toxic flower, a road leading to a wild animal's lair, an ambush on the bridge. Those are only a fraction of many ways you can abuse the element of surprise and anyone who dares enter without our permission will suffer from plenty of them.

Effects: Hostile Attrition: +100%.

Idea 7: Sykar's Codex

As much as Sykar the Great's reign laid grounds for a massive polity to emerge, so must the effort of his son Sykar the Lawgiver be preached, as he is the one who built a structure to preserve the state from near-fragmentation at the hand of squabbling tribes and Anzaran loyalists. He, unlike his father, integrated himself fully into the naga structures, brought the most influential scholars from across the cities and along with the High Priest Ikhaty codified the law to correct it in line with the morals of the Sculptors of Fate, making it so every lizard lives according to Anzalkatsa teachings.

Effects: global_autonomy：-0.05%.

Ambition: Rayaz Ambition

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Traditions: Three River Traditions

Effects: Hostile Attrition: +100%; Army morale: +15%.

Idea 1: Three River Tribes

Asarta, Arazin and Rayaz tribes are three ancient tribes, that inhabited the area between Zerat and Karassk for centuries. While for most of their history they were dependent on one of the great cities, and sometimes their overlords were different, tribes never forgot their bonds, which tied them close throughout centuries (placeholder)

Effects: Diplomatic reputation: +100% (inherited display; percentage conversion unverified).

Idea 2: Between Great Cities

All three tribes are located between Karassk and Zerat, which allows them control the trade between two wealthiest lizardfolk cities. (placeholder)

Effects: Caravan power: +20%.

Idea 3: Zianysha Warfare

Zianysha - are thin river boats lizardfolk learned to craft since time immemorial. However, river tribes learned to use them for quick movement and raids on their enemies, which allowed them to be a fearsome force near rivers. (placeholder)

Effects: Movement speed: +10%; Infantry combat ability: +5%.

Idea 4: Destined Conquerors

An old tale prophesies that once all three river tribes will be granted leaders, which will unite both Karassk and Zerat under their rule. (placeholder)

Effects: Land force limit modifier: +10%; global_manpower_modifier：+10%.

Idea 5: Boat Markets

Wondering bazaars on boats (placeholder)

Effects: Number of merchants: +1.

Idea 6: Naga Storytellers

Nagas educate youth of river tribes since time immemorial, and that earns them loyalty of river tribes (placeholder)

Effects: True faith tolerance: +2.

Idea 7: Metalworking Traditions

Huge deposits of metals supported long tradition of metalworking (placeholder)

Effects: Shock damage: +5%; Production efficiency: +5%.
